title: Normalized blowups preserve quasi-projectivity over an excellent affine base
statement:
Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $X$ admits a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_S$ for some $m\geq0$. Let $J\subset\mathcal O_X$ be a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $p:Z=\operatorname{Bl}_JX	o X$ for the ordinary blowup: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, its charts are $\operatorname{Spec}R[J/a]$, for nonzero members $a$ of a finite generating set, where $R[J/a]\subset\operatorname{Frac}R$ is generated by $R$ and $j/a$ for $j\in J$. Let $
u:N=Z^
u	o Z$ be normalization in the function field [def-sc-normalization]. Then $Z$ and $N$ are integral Noetherian schemes, where Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Both are of finite type over $S$ and admit locally closed immersions into finite-dimensional projective spaces over $S$. The morphism $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $p\circ
u:N	o X$ is projective in the global finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective] and birational, meaning an isomorphism between dense open subschemes.

source.place: Tags 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme); morphisms.tex Tags 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), 0C4M (lemma-composition-quasi-projective), 01VT (lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample); more-algebra.tex Tag 07QU (lemma-finite-type-over-excellent). Ordinary normalized-blowup consequence of these results.

proof.text: $S$ is Noetherian because it is the spectrum of the Noetherian ring $A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to S$. Thus $X$ is Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact.

Let $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_S$ be the given immersion. By [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension], applied to $\mathbf Z\to A$ and the graded isomorphism $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_m]\cong A[T_0,\ldots,T_m]$, the scheme $\mathbf P^m_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^m_{\mathbf Z}$ is identified over $S$ with $\operatorname{Proj}A[T_0,\ldots,T_m]$; we regard $i$ as an immersion into this Proj. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-shrink-to-closed-exists], its image is contained in a quasi-compact open $W$ of this Proj and $X\to W$ is closed. Apply [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] to obtain an ample invertible twist $\mathcal O_W(e)$ for some $e\geq1$. Its pullback to $X$ is ample by [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion]. Hence $X$ admits an ample invertible sheaf.

source.place: Tag 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj), (2),(3),(7); properties.tex Tag 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed). Quasi-compact closed neighbourhood as in the cited blueprint lemma.

proof.text: Form the sheaf Rees algebra $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J^n$ [def-nagata-sheaf-rees-algebra]. The degree-one inclusion $J\to\mathcal R$ extends by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] to $\operatorname{Sym}(J)\to\mathcal R$. It is graded and surjective: in degree $n$ every element of $J^n$ is locally a finite sum of products of $n$ sections of $J$, and each such product is the image of the corresponding symmetric monomial. Apply [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to get a closed immersion $\operatorname{Proj}_X\mathcal R\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_X(J)$. This source is the blowup in the statement: over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the standard chart for $at$ has coordinate ring $(R[Jt]_{at})_0=R[J/a]$, since $b t^n/(at)^n$ maps to $b/a^n$ for $b\in J^n$. The displayed maps commute with localization and with each other on overlaps, so identify the chart gluing over $X$. Consequently $p$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], using the finite-type quasi-coherent module $J$.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), proof via the symmetric-to-Rees surjection; constructions.tex Tag 07ZK (lemma-surjective-generated-degree-1-map-relative-proj).

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus V(J)$. It is nonempty and dense: a nonzero ideal subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$ on an integral scheme is nonzero at the generic point, since on any nonempty affine open its sections embed in the function field. On $U$ the ideal is the unit ideal, and the blowup charts are those of $U$ itself; hence $p^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism. Each chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[J/a]$ with $a\ne0$ has domain coordinate ring inside $\operatorname{Frac}R$, and its open $D(a)$ is nonempty and maps into $U$. Thus $p^{-1}U$ is dense in every chart, so dense in $Z$. All charts are reduced, and this dense open is irreducible because it is isomorphic to the nonempty open $U$ of the integral scheme $X$. Therefore $Z$ is reduced, irreducible and nonempty, hence integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]; $p$ is birational.

source.place: Tags 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme) and 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor); direct chart argument using the statement's rings.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper], $p$ is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Compose with $X\to S$ using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]; this makes $Z\to S$ finite type. Thus $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Choose the finite affine cover of $Z$ by finite-type $A$-algebras given by the definition of finite type. Each of these rings is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. By [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover], every affine coordinate ring of $Z$ is excellent.

Since $X$ has an ample invertible sheaf, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] upgrades $p$ to a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^r_X$ followed by projection for some $r\geq0$. Base change the given locally closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_S$ along $\mathbf P^r_S\to S$. Factoring $i$ as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] give an immersion $\mathbf P^r_X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^r_S\times_S\mathbf P^m_S$. Composition of immersions [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), followed by the closed Segre embedding [lem-chow-segre], gives a locally closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(r+1)(m+1)-1}_S$.

Apply the same explicit ample-sheaf construction to the immersion of $Z$ from Step 6. The Noetherian scheme $Z$ is quasi-compact, so [lemma-nagata-immersion-shrink-to-closed-exists] provides a quasi-compact open $W_Z$ of that projective space containing $Z$ as a closed subscheme. By [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension], as in Step 2, that projective space is $\operatorname{Proj}$ of the polynomial ring over $A$, so [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] supplies an ample invertible twist on $W_Z$. Pull it back by the closed immersion using [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion]. Thus $Z$ admits an ample invertible sheaf.

Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation] to the reduced Noetherian excellent scheme $Z$. For an integral scheme its componentwise normalization is its function-field normalization, because it has only one irreducible component [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Thus $
u:N	o Z$ is finite and surjective, $N$ is Noetherian excellent, and there is a dense open $O\subseteq Z$ over which $
u$ is an isomorphism. The scheme $N$ is integral: by [def-sc-normalization] the inverse image of an affine domain chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\overline B$, with $\overline B$ the integral closure of $B$ in $k(Z)$; these are domains, and their zero primes all glue to the same generic point with residue field $k(Z)$. Thus their union is reduced and irreducible. Finally a finite module algebra is generated as an algebra by its finite module generators, so [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] makes $
u$ finite type. Composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $N	o S$ finite type.

The finite map $
u$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. Since $Z$ admits an ample invertible sheaf (Step 7), [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $
u$ H-projective. Compose it with the H-projective map $p$ (Step 6), using [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], to obtain a closed immersion $N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^t_X$ over $X$. Base change $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_S$ along $\mathbf P^t_S	o S$ exactly as in Step 6, using stability of closed and open immersions under base change. Compose immersions and then the Segre closed immersion to obtain $N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(t+1)(m+1)-1}_S$. This proves both the required projectivity of $p
u$ and the quasi-projectivity of $N$ over $S$.

The two dense opens $O$ and $p^{-1}U$ of the integral scheme $Z$ have nonempty intersection $V$. The isomorphism $p^{-1}U\cong U$ identifies $V$ with a nonempty open $U_0\subset X$. The inverse image $
u^{-1}V$ is isomorphic to $V$ because $V\subset O$, and is a nonempty open of the integral scheme $N$. Both $U_0$ and $
u^{-1}V$ are therefore dense. The composite $p
u$ restricts to their isomorphism, which is the asserted birationality.

tool_uses.why: Embeds a product of two finite projective spaces in one; only this elementary projective geometry tool is used.
Excellence of finite-type affine A-algebras; the local unit has no permanence theorem.
Identifies P^m_S = Spec A x_Z P^m_Z with Proj A[T_0..T_m] (Stacks 01N2), so the Proj-open ample-twist lemma applies to the given embedding; added by the maintainer reader.
Restricts that ample twist to X and Z; no local unit lemma supplies it.
Promotes excellence of the selected affine cover to all affine coordinate rings, to match the normalization lemma.
A finite morphism embeds in a projective bundle; needed before converting normalization to H-projectivity.
Composes the two H-projective maps without asserting that local projectivity suffices.
An ample invertible twist on a quasi-compact open of polynomial Proj; supplies the ample base needed by 087S.
Projective-bundle morphisms are proper, hence finite type.
Converts projective bundles to finite-dimensional projective spaces using the explicitly constructed ample base.
Sheaf symmetric algebra and universal extension of J into the Rees algebra; not replaced by the log-resolution route.
Quasi-compact closed neighbourhood for an immersion; used to obtain an ample sheaf from the given quasi-projective embedding.
Surjective graded maps induce closed immersions; applies to the symmetric-to-Rees map and carries the ordinary blowup construction.
